name: Narmada
did_you_know: The Narmada is one of only two major peninsular rivers, along with the Tapi, that flows east to west into the Arabian Sea rather than east into the Bay of Bengal, running through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.
The Narmada Parikrama, a circumambulation of the entire river on foot along both banks, is a pilgrimage tradition said to take up to three years to complete.
The Sardar Sarovar Dam, one of independent India's most contested and consequential infrastructure projects, is built across the Narmada near Kevadia in Gujarat.
